fact: The Fourth Estate says Ghana's RTI law was passed in 2019 and requires public institutions to release information, and it counted 21 institutions that failed to release information in 24 requests, January 2025 to July 2026.
The RTI Commission acted under section 77(1) of the Right to Information Act, 2019 (Act 989), which requires public institutions to submit annual implementation reports.

The RTI Commission, in a press release of 5 August 2026, imposed administrative penalties of GHS 20,000 each on 254 public institutions for not filing 2025 annual RTI reports; the penalty is for missed reports, not a decision on a request.
GNA reports that Act 989 of 2019 operationalises the constitutional right of information and sets procedures for requesting information held by public institutions.
GNA reports that the Right to Information Commission, with a board chairman, exists and is empowered by the Act to oversee and enforce compliance, as of the 2026 stakeholders conference.
The RTI Commission announced its 2026 RTI Month programme to raise awareness of the Right to Information Act, 2019 (Act 989).
The Right to Information Commission's whole mandate is access to public information under the Right to Information Act, 2019 (Act 989).
Appropriation (No. 2) Act, 2025 (Act 1163) votes GHS 20,413,271 to the Right to Information Commission for 2026.
